title: I’ve just published a playable demo for my game:  Orbwalker - 100% AI Generated - Code and Assets.
author: Total-Trash8491
selftext:
I just posted a new early demo for **Orbwalker**, a fantasy match-3 roguelike where you drag orbs freely across the board, read enemy intent, build around relics and equipment, and try to survive each dungeon run.

The current demo shows the core loop:

* Free orb movement combat instead of fixed tile swapping
* Enemy intent and turn-based tactical decisions
* Shops, relic choices, equipment, and run summaries
* A mobile-first interface designed for fast dungeon runs

Demo video:  
[https://www.youtube.com/shorts/IIFmoNhv2NM](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/IIFmoNhv2NM)

Playable demo:  
[https://rajahafify.itch.io/orbwalker](https://rajahafify.itch.io/orbwalker)

The interesting part from an AI game dev angle is that the project was built almost entirely through OpenAI tools over about one month of development.

* Code was generated with OpenAI GPT-5.5
* Art assets were made with OpenAI image generation through Codex workflows
* Music was generated programmatically as MIDI, then converted to WAV using Python
* Development used OpenAI Pro subscriptions throughout the process

One question I’m still thinking about: if an AI writes the code that generates a MIDI file, should the resulting music be considered an AI-generated asset, a procedurally generated asset, or both?

I’d really appreciate feedback on:

* Combat feel
* Clarity of enemy intent and player choices
* Pacing
* UI readability on mobile
* What systems or content you’d want to see next

Would also love to hear how others here are classifying AI-assisted procedural music or assets in their own projects.

I dont think you need more content, I think you need to improve what you have currently. Solid base for a generic matching puzzle game, just have to polish it now

comments.author: miomao10
comments.body: Good concept: my issue: when merging matches the screen stops you from playing. This is bad- I should be able to play and play and play and not be stoped, my combos should show damage easily so the screen doesn’t pause

replies.author: Total-Trash8491
replies.body: There is an option to make vfx resolved instantly. You can give it a try, but it looks terrible

replies.author: miomao10
replies.body: I don’t understand, we are using ai to make these games- can’t you tell the ai to polish it, show it some other games that have clear matching. If you are using Claude/codex you can tell it specially what to look and do so it’s not reading the whole codebase and costing you. This should be a polish round for the ai. It can really do the work if you describe it right. I suggest using readme and claud.md - you want to trap the ai in context relevant to the fixes. Not just tell the ai- fix the issue. Ask your ai to build a manager for your game. Ask it to review everything and create documents for your game and other ai. Then ask it to fix this issue specially and ask it to chip the message- Claude ai will start a new chat just for this issue in the relevant area and not waste tokens after this set up

replies.author: Total-Trash8491
replies.body:
To be honest I personally disagree with your take that player should be allowed to make matches continously. Like in balatro, after you make a hand, even in the fastest settings, you can see the calculation happening. Which I feel, add to the juice. But I also agree that the downtime between matches doesn't feel good. That is why I added the options for the speed of the vfx (no other settings is added yet). 


Btw, I don't have problem with getting Codex to work on specific task. I do have AGENTS.md file tuned to my specific projects.  In my personal testing with this project, it's really hard to get to LLM to polish something that is not language based ( like game juice and taste). Especially when it comes to animations and timing. I had codex running for 16 hours once to work on vfx and the results is worse than the svg animations I have now.

replies.author: miomao10
replies.body: Interesting. I still think the ai could figure out your wants. Good luck with your project!

replies.author: miomao10
replies.body: I am developing a merge 2 game and described the mechanics very specially and it actually plays great no issues. You want smooth buttery for the player- anything else usually gets the X
